function.name: hotel_booking
function.description: Books a hotel room given the location, room type, stay duration and any additional preferences. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city where you want to book the hotel.

room_type.description: Type of the room required. Options: 'single', 'double', 'deluxe', etc.

duration.description: The number of nights you want to book the hotel for.

start_date.description: The date when your stay begins.

preferences.description: Optional preferences of stay at the hotel. Default to use all if not specified.

message.reasoning: The user wants to book a pet-friendly single room in Manhattan, NY, starting March 10, 2023 for 3 nights. We need to call the function hotel_booking with location "New York Manhattan" or "Manhattan, New York". The room_type "single". duration 3. start_date "2023-03-10". preferences: "pet_friendly". The function signature expects preferences?: "pet_friendly" | "gym" | "swimming_pool" | "free_breakfast" | "parking"[]; Wait preferences is optional and type is "pet_friendly" | "gym" | "swimming_pool" | "free_breakfast" | "parking"[]; That seems ambiguous: It might be a union of string or array? The description says "Optional preferences of stay at the hotel. Default to use all if not specified." So maybe preferences can be an array of strings. But the type says "pet_friendly" | "gym" | "swimming_pool" | "free_breakfast" | "parking"[]; That is weird: "parking"[] means array of parking? Actually maybe they want an array of strings. We'll pass preferences: ["pet_friendly"]. That should satisfy. Let's call the function.
